extracted.intended_audience: general readers, film enthusiasts, and researchers looking for encyclopedic information about the film The Big Short
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article describing the 2015 film The Big Short, its production, plot, cast, release, reception, historical accuracy, and awards — useful as an overview and as implicit evaluative criteria for the film.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performances (acting)
rubrics_metrics.description: A critical and commercial success, the film received acclaim for the performances of the cast (particularly those of Bale and Carell). Christian Bale received widespread acclaim, earning an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor nomination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance quality is a principal evaluative axis for the film — reviewers singled out lead performances (Bale, Carell) as central strengths; awards nominations and wins for actors serve as indicators of acting quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direction
rubrics_metrics.description: The film received acclaim for McKay's direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direction is highlighted as a key factor in the film's success; assessors should consider tone, pacing, and the director's choices (including use of cameos and inventive explanatory devices) when evaluating the film.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing
rubrics_metrics.description: The film received acclaim for editing and was nominated for Best Film Editing; Hank Corwin won the American Cinema Editors Award for Best Edited Feature Film (Comedy or Musical).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editing is singled out as an element contributing to clarity and energy in telling a complicated story; awards and nominations are used as evidence of editorial quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screenplay / Adapted Screenplay
rubrics_metrics.description: The film won the Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay (Adam McKay and Charles Randolph). Screenwriter Charles Randolph and director McKay discussed finding the 'right tone' for the film.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation of the screenplay should consider fidelity to source material, narrative structure, and especially tone: the filmmakers sought a tone 'slightly funnier than your average Miloš Forman comedy' — balancing character-based grounding with satirical elements. The rewrites and deliberate inclusion of explanatory cameos are production choices tied to the screenplay's effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and Approach (balancing comedy and seriousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: The film is described as a 'biographical comedy drama' that 'approaches a serious, complicated subject with an impressive attention to detail' and delivers 'a well-acted, scathingly funny indictment' of real-life villains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors should judge how well the film balances humor and gravity, whether the comedic approach clarifies or undercuts the subject, and whether the chosen tone supports character arcs and the underlying plot of financial collapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of celebrity cameos / explanatory devices
rubrics_metrics.description: McKay's idea to include celebrity cameos in the film to explain the financial concepts; Margot Robbie appears to explain mortgage-backed securities, Anthony Bourdain to detail CDOs, Richard Thaler and Selena Gomez to describe credit default swaps and synthetic CDOs. Michael Burry appears in a cameo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The film's pedagogical devices (cameos, interstitial explanations) are an explicit production choice intended to make complex financial mechanisms accessible; evaluation should consider clarity, effectiveness, and whether such devices fit the film's tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Information Is Beautiful deduced the film was 91.4% accurate when compared to real-life events, noting 'very little dramatization or fakery.' Critics with finance backgrounds generally agreed the film was accurate while taking creative license into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess historical fidelity by comparing dramatized events and character portrayals to documented facts; the page notes name changes and some biographical modifications but overall substantial accuracy. The epilogue and critics' commentary are offered as context for accuracy judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Casting choices and portrayal fidelity
rubrics_metrics.description: Many character names have been changed and some biographical information slightly modified. Steve Eisman (the real figure behind Mark Baum) said Carell's portrayal was 'accurate enough' though not literally him; later Eisman reassessed and said Carell's anger reflected reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should consider whether casting and portrayals capture essential traits and whether narrative/name changes materially affect fidelity or audience understanding; direct comments from real-life counterparts are cited as evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box office and commercial performance
rubrics_metrics.description: The film grossed $133.4 million worldwide on a $50 million budget; it set per-screen gross records on limited release and had notable opening and weekend grosses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial success is presented as an evaluative metric: profitability, per-screen averages, and release strategy (limited then wide) provide measures of market reception and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate critical reception metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Rotten Tomatoes: 89% approval based on 331 reviews (average 7.8/10). Metacritic: score of 81/100 indicating 'universal acclaim'. CinemaScore: A−. IGN: 8.6/10. The New York Times praised the film's explanatory power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use aggregator scores, average ratings, and major outlet reviews as collective indicators of critical consensus and to identify aspects critics highlighted (attention to detail, clarity, entertainment value).

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and nominations
rubrics_metrics.description: Won Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay; nominated for Best Picture, Best Director, Best Supporting Actor (Bale), Best Film Editing; nominated/won multiple Golden Globe, BAFTA, WGA, Critics' Choice, ACE Eddie, Producers Guild, National Board of Review and other awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards and nominations across organizations are presented as downstream validation of excellence in screenplay, acting, directing, editing, and overall film quality; they serve as formal evaluative signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: MPA rating / content suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: The film was rated R by the Motion Picture Association for pervasive language and some sexuality/nudity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rating provides a content-suitability criterion for audiences and programmers and may factor into evaluations tied to audience reach and marketing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production authenticity (locations and recreation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal photography began in New Orleans; production recreated the offices of Lehman Brothers in the lobby of the New York State Department of Financial Services. Filming locations include New Orleans, Manhattan, and other on-location choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production decisions (on-location shooting, set recreation) are relevant to assessments of authenticity and period/atmosphere; such choices are evidence used when judging the film's production values and verisimilitude.
